bias.comment: Ray-tracing offset for primary ray origin
bias.name: bias

map_factor.comment: Increase or decrease the internal position map buffer resolution
map_factor.label: map factor
map_factor.name: map_factor

mb_shutter_bias.comment: Biases the motion blur samples toward one end of the shutter interval.
mb_shutter_bias.label: mb shutter bias
mb_shutter_bias.name: mb_shutter_bias

mb_shutter_close.comment: Frame at which the shutter closes, i.e., the end of the motion blur interval.
mb_shutter_close.label: mb shutter close
mb_shutter_close.name: mb_shutter_close

mb_shutter_open.comment: Frame at which the shutter opens, i.e., the beginning of the motion blur interval.
mb_shutter_open.label: mb shutter open
mb_shutter_open.name: mb_shutter_open

medium_geometry.comment: The geometry the camera is 'inside' to which you'd like the medium_material applied. (The use case for this is typically partially-submerged cameras)
medium_geometry.label: medium geometry
medium_geometry.name: medium_geometry

medium_material.comment: The material the camera is 'inside'. If no medium_geometry is specified, ALL rays will have this initial index of refraction applied.
medium_material.label: medium material
medium_material.name: medium_material

modo_render_camera.comment: Render through this camera, from where this item stands, instead of the Modo camera.
modo_render_camera.label: render through this camera
modo_render_camera.name: modo_render_camera

normal_map.comment: Use this option to supply your own normals that are used when computing ray directions. Without this option, normals are computed from the geometry and do not take into account any material applied normal mapping.
normal_map.label: normal map
normal_map.name: normal_map

normal_map_space.comment: Use camera space if you generated per frame normal maps in a pre-pass using the normal material aov. You probably want to use tangent space if you are using a normal map that is also used in the surfacing setup.
normal_map_space.label: normal map space
normal_map_space.name: normal_map_space

pixel_sample_map.comment: Map indicating the number of pixel samples that should be used per pixel (in uniform sampling mode). This is a multiplier on the global pixel sample count specified in SceneVariables. If the provided map has incompatible dimensions, it will be resized.
pixel_sample_map.label: pixel sample map
pixel_sample_map.name: pixel_sample_map

use_relative_bias.comment: If true, bias is scaled based on position magnitude
use_relative_bias.label: use relative bias
use_relative_bias.name: use_relative_bias

uv_attribute.comment: Specifies a Vec2f primitive attribute to use as the uv coordinates. If empty, the default uv for the mesh is used. The uvs must provide a unique parameterization of the mesh, i.e. a given (u, v) can appear only once on the mesh being baked.
uv_attribute.label: uv attribute
uv_attribute.name: uv_attribute

color.comment: Color within the Barn Door lit region. For each color channel 0 is full shadow and 1 is no shadow.
color.label: color
color.name: color

density.comment: Fades the filter effect. 0 means no effect (like having no filter), and 1 means full effect.
density.name: density

edge.comment: The size of the transition zone from the rounded box to the outside, as a proportion of width (or height, whichever is smaller).
edge.name: edge

edge_scale_bottom.comment: The scale factor for the bottom edge.
edge_scale_bottom.label: edge scale bottom
edge_scale_bottom.name: edge_scale_bottom

edge_scale_left.comment: The scale factor for the left edge.
edge_scale_left.label: edge scale left
edge_scale_left.name: edge_scale_left

edge_scale_right.comment: The scale factor for the right edge.
edge_scale_right.label: edge scale right
edge_scale_right.name: edge_scale_right

edge_scale_top.comment: The scale factor for the top edge.
edge_scale_top.label: edge scale top
edge_scale_top.name: edge_scale_top

invert.comment: Swap application of the filter from inside the Barn Door to outside.
invert.name: invert

mode.comment: Analytical mode allows light to shading points that project to the flap opening. Physical mode allows light whose direction goes through the flap opening.
mode.name: mode

pre_barn_distance.comment: The distance from the BarnDoorLightFilter that the pre_barn_mode control takes effect.
pre_barn_distance.name: pre_barn_distance

pre_barn_mode.comment: Force the region before the pre_barn_distance to be fully filtered (black), not filtered at all (white), or treated the same as elsewhere (default).
pre_barn_mode.label: pre barn mode
pre_barn_mode.name: pre_barn_mode

projector_focal_distance.comment: The distance of the flap opening from the projector origin. Ignored for orthographic projection.
projector_focal_distance.label: projector focal distance
projector_focal_distance.name: projector_focal_distance

projector_height.comment: The height of the frustum at distance 1.0.
projector_height.label: height of the flap opening
projector_height.name: projector_height

projector_type.comment: The projection type used to map points to the flap opening. Perspective has a focal point, while orthographic does not.
projector_type.label: projector type
projector_type.name: projector_type

projector_width.comment: The width of the frustum at distance 1.0.
projector_width.label: width of the flap opening
projector_width.name: projector_width

radius.comment: The radius by which to convert the base box shape into a rounded box, as a proportion of half the width (or height, whichever is smaller).
radius.name: radius

rotation.comment: The angle to rotate the Barn Door counter-clockwise as seen from the light, in degrees.
rotation.name: rotation

size_bottom.comment: Additional size on the bottom edge.
size_bottom.name: size_bottom

size_left.comment: Additional size on the left edge.
size_left.name: size_left

size_right.comment: Additional size on the right edge.
size_right.name: size_right

size_top.comment: Additional size on the top edge.
size_top.name: size_top

use_light_xform.comment: Attach the filter to the light (in the -Z direction) and ignore node_xform.
use_light_xform.label: use light xform
use_light_xform.name: use_light_xform

anisotropy.comment: Value in the interval [-1,1] that defines how foward (1) or backward (-1) scattering the volume is. A value of 0.0 indicates an isotropic volume.
anisotropy.name: anisotropy

attenuation_color.comment: A color to tint (multiply to) the attenuation. Technically the product of attenuation color and intensity is the attenuation (extinction) coefficient.(Note the inverse behavior of color with this parameter.)
attenuation_color.label: attenuation color
attenuation_color.name: attenuation_color

attenuation_factor.comment: Identical in behavior to attenuation_intensity but provided as a second means to control attenuation, intended for use during lighting as a per-shot or per-sequence adjustment.
attenuation_factor.label: attenuation factor
attenuation_factor.name: attenuation_factor

attenuation_intensity.comment: The rate at which the light traversing a volume is attenuated. The attenuation (extinction) coefficient is the product of attenuation_color, attenuation_intensity, and attenuation_factor
attenuation_intensity.label: attenuation intensity
attenuation_intensity.name: attenuation_intensity

attenuation_max_depth.comment: Represents the maximum ray depth, or the longest visible distance a ray has to travel through the volume. This sets the upper bound for the ramp.
attenuation_max_depth.label: attenuation max depth
attenuation_max_depth.name: attenuation_max_depth

attenuation_min_depth.comment: Represents the minimum ray depth, or the shortest visible distance a ray has to travel through the volume. This sets the lower bound for the ramp.
attenuation_min_depth.label: attenuation min depth
attenuation_min_depth.name: attenuation_min_depth

bake_divisions.comment: Divide widest axis by this many divisions
bake_divisions.name: bake_divisions

bake_resolution_mode.comment: Method to specify grid resolution of baked density grid. Choices are: \t\t"default": For shaders that are bound to vdb volumes, use vdb resolution. \t\t\t\t\t\tFor shaders that are bounds to mesh geometries use 100 divisions \t\t"divisions": Specify number of divisions. \t\t"voxel size": Specify voxel size.
bake_resolution_mode.label: bake resolution mode
bake_resolution_mode.name: bake_resolution_mode

bake_voxel_size.comment: Size of voxel in world space
bake_voxel_size.name: bake_voxel_size

density_max_depth.comment: Represents the maximum ray depth, or the longest visible distance a ray has to travel through the volume. This sets the upper bound for the ramp.
density_max_depth.label: max depth
density_max_depth.name: density_max_depth

density_min_depth.comment: Represents the minimum ray depth, or the shortest visible distance a ray has to travel through the volume. This sets the lower bound for the ramp.
density_min_depth.label: min depth
density_min_depth.name: density_min_depth

diffuse_color.comment: Reflectance color of the volume. Technically this is called scattering albedo, which is the scattering coefficient divided by the extinction coefficient.
diffuse_color.label: diffuse color
diffuse_color.name: diffuse_color

diffuse_max_depth.comment: Represents the maximum ray depth, or the longest visible distance a ray has to travel through the volume. This sets the upper bound for the ramp.
diffuse_max_depth.label: max depth
diffuse_max_depth.name: diffuse_max_depth

diffuse_min_depth.comment: Represents the minimum ray depth, or the shortest visible distance a ray has to travel through the volume. This sets the lower bound for the ramp.
diffuse_min_depth.label: min depth
diffuse_min_depth.name: diffuse_min_depth

emission_color.comment: A color multiplier for the emission. The product of emission color and intensity is the emission coefficient
emission_color.label: emission color
emission_color.name: emission_color

emission_intensity.comment: The rate at which a volume emits light at a given point. The product of emission color and intensity is the emission coefficient.
emission_intensity.label: emission intensity
emission_intensity.name: emission_intensity

match_diffuse.comment: Use the same color(s) for attenuation that is/are being used for diffuse.
match_diffuse.label: match diffuse color(s)
match_diffuse.name: match_diffuse

surface_opacity_threshold.comment: Accumulated opacity that's considered the 'surface' for computing surface position and Z
surface_opacity_threshold.name: surface_opacity_threshold

use_attenuation_ramp.comment: Use a ramp to define different attenuation colors depending on the depth of the volume.
use_attenuation_ramp.label: use ramp
use_attenuation_ramp.name: use_attenuation_ramp

use_diffuse_ramp.comment: Use a ramp to define different diffuse colors depending on the depth of the volume.
use_diffuse_ramp.label: use ramp
use_diffuse_ramp.name: use_diffuse_ramp

contains_camera.comment: Specifies whether the geometry contains the camera and should be used for IOR tracking. This should not be changed by the user -- they should instead attach the relevant geometry to the camera, which will then flag this geometry.
contains_camera.name: contains_camera

dicing_camera.comment: Alternate camera that is used for adaptive tessellation. This is useful if you want adaptive tessellation to behave consistently in a sequence, regardless of what the main camera is doing
dicing_camera.name: dicing_camera

label.comment: label used in material aov expresssions
label.name: label

modo_material.comment: The material tag of the Modo material this is rendered with; empty for the base material.
modo_material.label: material tag
modo_material.name: modo_material

modo_volume.comment: The name of a MoonRay volume item that fills this shape.
modo_volume.label: volume
modo_volume.name: modo_volume

ray_epsilon.comment: When a secondary ray is fired, anything within this distance of the intersection point will be ignored. Instead, it is considered part of the current intersection's geometry. If zero, an automatically calculated epsilon will be used.
ray_epsilon.label: ray epsilon
ray_epsilon.name: ray_epsilon

references.comment: list of geometries that geometry procedural can reference during procedural generate/update stages. For example, an instancer geometry procedural can instance primitives generated by the reference geometry procedural.
references.name: references

reverse_normals.comment: enable to reverse the normals in the geometry
reverse_normals.label: reverse normals
reverse_normals.name: reverse_normals

shadow_exclusion_mappings.comment: A space-separated list of mappings of the form A:B where: A is a comma-separated list of names of parts of this Geometry, or an asterisk to specify the whole geometry; B is a comma-separated list of shadow receiver set labels established using the ["shadow_receiver_label"] attribute, or an asterisk to specify to all such sets in the scene. For each of the listed mappings, shadows from the parts specified in A will be suppressed from casting onto any geometries in the ShadowReceiverSets specified in B. **Note: no part name should appear more than once in the string, otherwise the behavior is undefined.**
shadow_exclusion_mappings.name: shadow_exclusion_mappings

shadow_ray_epsilon.comment: When a shadow ray is fired, anything within this distance of the intersection point will be ignored. If this value is less than "ray_epsilon", then it has no additional effect.
shadow_ray_epsilon.label: shadow ray epsilon
shadow_ray_epsilon.name: shadow_ray_epsilon

shadow_receiver_label.comment: Label used to associate Geometry objects into ShadowReceiverSets. Using this in combination with the ["shadow_exclusion_mappings"] attribute, shadows from specified geometries or their parts can be suppressed from casting shadows onto one or more specified sets.
shadow_receiver_label.name: shadow_receiver_label

side_type.comment: set single sidedness of the mesh, will affect the visibility of the mesh based on normal direction
side_type.label: side type
side_type.name: side_type

static.comment: disable if the geometry will be updated between frames
static.name: static

use_local_camera_motion_blur.comment: Enables experimental feature that also attempts to remove the camera blur in the local regions
use_local_camera_motion_blur.label: use local camera motion blur
use_local_camera_motion_blur.name: use_local_camera_motion_blur

use_local_motion_blur.comment: Enables the local motion blur feature, which makes the geometry procedural responsible for handling all of the geometry's motion and allows for custom effects
use_local_motion_blur.label: use local motion blur
use_local_motion_blur.name: use_local_motion_blur

visible_diffuse_reflection.comment: whether the geometry is visible in diffuse reflection
visible_diffuse_reflection.label: visible diffuse reflection
visible_diffuse_reflection.name: visible_diffuse_reflection

visible_diffuse_transmission.comment: whether the geometry is visible in diffuse transmission
visible_diffuse_transmission.label: visible diffuse transmission
visible_diffuse_transmission.name: visible_diffuse_transmission

visible_glossy_reflection.comment: whether the geometry is visible in glossy reflection.
visible_glossy_reflection.label: visible glossy reflection
visible_glossy_reflection.name: visible_glossy_reflection

visible_glossy_transmission.comment: whether the geometry is visible in glossy transmission (refraction).
visible_glossy_transmission.label: visible glossy transmission
visible_glossy_transmission.name: visible_glossy_transmission

visible_in_camera.comment: whether the geometry is visible to camera rays
visible_in_camera.label: visible in camera
visible_in_camera.name: visible_in_camera

visible_mirror_reflection.comment: whether the geometry is visible in miror reflection.
visible_mirror_reflection.label: visible mirror reflection
visible_mirror_reflection.name: visible_mirror_reflection

visible_mirror_transmission.comment: whether the geometry is visible in miror transmission (refraction).
visible_mirror_transmission.label: visible mirror transmission
visible_mirror_transmission.name: visible_mirror_transmission

visible_volume.comment: whether the geometry is visible in indirect volume rays
visible_volume.label: visible volume
visible_volume.name: visible_volume

begin_distance.comment: Where the ramp starts relative to the light or the ramp's independent transform
begin_distance.name: begin_distance

colors.comment: Vector of colors specified at different distances
colors.label: colors
colors.name: colors

distances.comment: Distances between which colors are interpolated
distances.label: distances
distances.name: distances

end_distance.comment: Where the ramp ends relative to the light or the ramp's independent transform
end_distance.name: end_distance

interpolation_types.comment: Interpolation types between the specified distances. 0: None 1: linear 2: exponential_up 3: exponential_down 4: smooth 5: catmull_rom
interpolation_types.label: interpolation types
interpolation_types.name: interpolation_types

mode.comment: Ramp: Radiates out from the center of the light or ramp location. Directional: Linear starting at the location of the light or ramp location along negative z
mode.name: mode

use_xform.comment: The filter can be bound to a light or lights position or when this toggle is set, can have its own transform
use_xform.label: use xform
use_xform.name: use_xform

wrap_mode.comment: For directional filter mode where filter uses distance along -Z axis. Extend: f(z) = f(0) for z > 0. Mirror: f(z) = f(-z).
wrap_mode.name: wrap_mode

light_filters.comment: List of light filters to combine together
light_filters.name: light_filters

mode.comment: How the light filters are combined
mode.name: mode

blur_far_value.comment: Blur filter radius (in texture UV space) at the far distance
blur_far_value.name: blur_far_value

blur_mid_value.comment: Blur filter radius (in texture UV space) at the mid distance
blur_mid_value.name: blur_mid_value

blur_near_value.comment: Blur filter radius (in texture UV space) at the near distance
blur_near_value.name: blur_near_value

density.comment: Controls how much of the cookie is added to the light
density.name: density

outside_projection.comment: What happens outside the frustum of the projection camera. Black (default), White, or Default (This uses the mode set on the Moonray map shader)
outside_projection.name: outside_projection

projector.comment: If a projector is specified, it overrides the node_xform and projector_* attributes
projector.name: projector

projector_film_width_aperture.comment: Size of the camera image plane
projector_film_width_aperture.name: projector_film_width_aperture

projector_focal.comment: Focal length of the lens when using perspective projection
projector_focal.name: projector_focal

texture_map.comment: Moonray map. Any Moonray map generator, checkerboard, noise, image map. You may also add any of the map modifiers, color correct for example. The default is an image map.
texture_map.name: texture_map

blur_far_value.comment: Blur filter radius (in texture UV space) at the far distance
blur_far_value.name: blur_far_value

blur_mid_value.comment: Blur filter radius (in texture UV space) at the mid distance
blur_mid_value.name: blur_mid_value

blur_near_value.comment: Blur filter radius (in texture UV space) at the near distance
blur_near_value.name: blur_near_value

density.comment: Controls how much of the cookie is added to the light
density.name: density

gamma.comment: Per-channel gamma used in color-correcting the light filter's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel: For input > 0, output = pow(input, gamma) For input <= 0, output = input
gamma.name: gamma

outside_projection.comment: What happens outside the frustum of the projection camera. Black (default), White, or Default (This uses the mode set on the Moonray map shader)
outside_projection.name: outside_projection

projector.comment: If a projector is specified, it overrides the node_xform and projector_* attributes
projector.name: projector

projector_film_width_aperture.comment: Size of the camera image plane
projector_film_width_aperture.name: projector_film_width_aperture

projector_focal.comment: Focal length of the lens when using perspective projection
projector_focal.name: projector_focal

texture.comment: File name of the texture applied to the light filter. Any file format supported by OpenImageIO can be used.
texture.name: texture

bake_divisions.comment: Divide widest axis by this many divisions
bake_divisions.name: bake_divisions

bake_resolution_mode.comment: Method to specify grid resolution of baked density grid. Choices are: \t\t"default": For shaders that are bound to vdb volumes, use vdb resolution. \t\t\t\t\t\tFor shaders that are bounds to mesh geometries use 100 divisions \t\t"divisions": Specify number of divisions. \t\t"voxel size": Specify voxel size.
bake_resolution_mode.label: bake resolution mode
bake_resolution_mode.name: bake_resolution_mode

bake_voxel_size.comment: Size of voxel in world space
bake_voxel_size.name: bake_voxel_size

indirect_volume.comment: The volume to cutout / use for indirect illumination and occlusion. Cutout behavior is invoked for primary rays but secondary/indirect rays are processed normally.
indirect_volume.name: indirect_volume

surface_opacity_threshold.comment: Accumulated opacity that's considered the 'surface' for computing surface position and Z
surface_opacity_threshold.name: surface_opacity_threshold

apply_scene_scale.comment: Whether to apply scene scale variable when normalized.
apply_scene_scale.name: apply_scene_scale

color.comment: The light's RGB values. These are combined multiplicatively with the intensity and other attributes in determining the light's 3-channel radiance.
color.name: color

contrast.comment: Per-channel contrast used in color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. The operation mimics Nuke's ColorCorrect node's contrast function: For input > 0, output = 0.18 * pow(inputCompnent/0.18, contrast). For input <= 0, output = 0.18 * input * pow(1/0.18, contrast).
contrast.name: contrast

exposure.comment: The light's exposure value. This value provides an alternative to the intensity value as a mechanism for controlling the light's overall brightness, and is inspired by the corresponding photographic term but is generalised to apply independently to each light. To calculate its effect, pow(2, exposure) is combined multiplicatively with the color and other attributes in determining the light's 3-channel radiance.
exposure.name: exposure

gain.comment: Per-channel gain used in tandem with a per-channel offset for color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel: output = input * gain + offset
gain.name: gain

gamma.comment: Per-channel gamma used in color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel: For input > 0, output = pow(input, gamma) For input <= 0, output = input
gamma.name: gamma

height.comment: The height of the cylinder as measured along its axis.
height.name: height

intensity.comment: The light's intensity. This is combined multiplicatively with the color and other attributes in determining the light's 3-channel radiance.
intensity.name: intensity

label.comment: Label used in light aov expressions.
label.name: label

light_filters.comment: Vector of LightFilters associated with the light.
light_filters.label: light filters
light_filters.name: light_filters

max_shadow_distance.comment: The distance from the light beyond which a light-receiving surface will no longer receive shadows cast from that light. Note that the distance is thresholded for each occlusion ray cast for this light, it is possible for a receiving point to lie at an intermediate distance such that some parts of the light are closer than the threshold distance and other parts beyond it, in which case the point will appearto be in partial shadow.
max_shadow_distance.name: max_shadow_distance

mb.comment: Whether motion-blur is active for this light. When set to true, the scene's illumination will correctly account for any blur() applied to the light's transformation matrix.
mb.name: mb

min_shadow_distance.comment: The distance from the light before which a light-receiving surface will no longer receive shadows cast from that light. Note that the distance is thresholded for each occlusion ray cast for this light, it is possible for a receiving point to lie at an intermediate distance such that some parts of the light are closer than the threshold distance and other parts beyond it, in which case the point will appearto be in partial shadow.
min_shadow_distance.name: min_shadow_distance

normalized.comment: When set to true, the size of the light can be changed without altering the amount of total energy cast into the scene. This is achieved via scaling the light's radiance by the reciprocal of its surface area. When set to false, the radiance is used as-is, regardless of surface area.
normalized.name: normalized

offset.comment: Per-channel offset used in tandem with a per-channel gain for color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel: output = input * gain + offset
offset.name: offset

on.comment: Whether the light is switched on.
on.name: on

presence_shadows.comment: Switch this attribute on for shadows cast from this light to correctly respect presence values. When off, surfaces with a material with presence less than 1.0 will cast opaque shadows from this light. This is an optimization - when the attribute is off, occlusion rays (fast) are used for testing for shadows. When it is on, regular rays (slower) are used, and the material's presence is evaluated to determine how much shadowing should occur. When set to "use default" it reads from the value of SceneVariable enable_presence_shadows.
presence_shadows.label: presence shadows
presence_shadows.name: presence_shadows

ray_termination.comment: Whether the light is used for ray termination color. Ray termination color is used for filling in falsely dark areas where ray paths have been terminated too early by the depth controls. Such a ray path immediately exits to any ray termination light(s) present in the light set being applied to the lobe, ignoring occlusion by scene geometry. Any light can either be a regular light or a ray termination light (but not both). Thus they can be freely assigned to light sets, which provides a mechanism for applying specific ray termination lights to specific materials, parts or objects. Ray termination color is only applied to non-hair transmission lobes.
ray_termination.name: ray_termination

saturation.comment: Per-channel saturation used in color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel: output = lerp(luminance(inputRGB), input, saturation).
saturation.name: saturation

sidedness.comment: When set to 0 (regular), light is emitted from the outward-facing surface of the cylinder. When set to 1 (reverse), light is emitted from the inward-facing surface of the cylinder. There is no mode for emitting from both surfaces at the same time, but two cylinder lights of opposing sidedness can be combined to achieve this effect.
sidedness.name: sidedness

temperature.comment: Color temperature using Nuke-style T/M/I settings (T = temperature, M = magenta/green, I = intensity). This is achieved as follows: The 3-channel temperature is interpreted as the vector (T,M,I). The followiong scale values are then applied to the RGB components: outputR = inputR * (pow(2,I) + M/3 - T/2) outputG = inputG * (pow(2,I) - 2*M/3 outputB = inputB * (pow(2,I) + M/3 + T/2)
temperature.name: temperature

texture.comment: File name of the texture applied to the light. If set to the empty string, no texture is applied. Any file format supported by OpenImageIO can be used. The texture is used in 2 ways - for looking up the texture value at the intersection point when a ray hits the light, and for building a lookup-table-based auxilliary data structure used for distributing light samples over the texture.
texture.name: texture

texture_border_color.comment: RGB value used when a texture lookup occurs outside the texture.
texture_border_color.name: texture_border_color

texture_coverage.comment: Texture scales in the u and v-directions.
texture_coverage.name: texture_coverage

texture_filter.comment: The filtering mode to apply to the texture. Nearest neighbor is the cheapest filtering mode but produces a blocky result. Switch linear filtering on for a smoother result. Additionally, mip-mapping can be switched on with either nearest neighbor or linear filtering.
texture_filter.label: texture filter
texture_filter.name: texture_filter

texture_mirror_u.comment: Whether to mirror the texture in the u-direction. If set to false, the texture is repeated in the u-direction.
texture_mirror_u.name: texture_mirror_u

texture_mirror_v.comment: Whether to mirror the texture in the v-direction. If set to false, the texture is repeated in the v-direction.
texture_mirror_v.name: texture_mirror_v

texture_reps_u.comment: Number of times texture repeats in u over the scaled texture space.
texture_reps_u.name: texture_reps_u

texture_reps_v.comment: Number of times texture repeats in v over the scaled texture space.
texture_reps_v.name: texture_reps_v

texture_translation.comment: Translation of the texture in (u,v)-space, in units of the texture size. For example, a translation of (0.25, 0.5) will translate the texture one-quarter of its width in the u-direction and one-half of its height in the v-direction.
texture_translation.name: texture_translation

visible_diffuse_reflection.comment: Whether the light is visible in diffuse reflection.
visible_diffuse_reflection.label: visible diffuse reflection
visible_diffuse_reflection.name: visible_diffuse_reflection

visible_diffuse_transmission.comment: Whether the light is visible in diffuse transmission.
visible_diffuse_transmission.label: visible diffuse transmission
visible_diffuse_transmission.name: visible_diffuse_transmission

visible_glossy_reflection.comment: Whether the light is visible in glossy reflection.
visible_glossy_reflection.label: visible glossy reflection
visible_glossy_reflection.name: visible_glossy_reflection

visible_glossy_transmission.comment: Whether the light is visible in glossy transmission (refraction).

focal_plane_distance.comment: The distance from the SpotLight's position, measured in the direction the light is pointing, at which the projected image will be in focus.
focal_plane_distance.label: focal plane distance
focal_plane_distance.name: focal_plane_distance

gain.comment: Per-channel gain used in tandem with a per-channel offset for color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel: output = input * gain + offset
gain.name: gain

gamma.comment: Per-channel gamma used in color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel: For input > 0, output = pow(input, gamma) For input <= 0, output = input
gamma.name: gamma

inner_cone_angle.comment: The apex angle of the bright inner cone of the light emitted by the SpotLight. Full illumination takes place inside this region. This is a full angle, measured from one side to the other. There is a falloff function applied between the outer and inner cones - see the angle_falloff_type attribute.
inner_cone_angle.label: inner cone angle
inner_cone_angle.name: inner_cone_angle

intensity.comment: The light's intensity. This is combined multiplicatively with the color and other attributes in determining the light's 3-channel radiance.
intensity.name: intensity

label.comment: Label used in light aov expressions.
label.name: label

lens_radius.comment: The radius of the SpotLight's lens (when the aspect ratio is 1.0, so that the lens is circular).
lens_radius.label: lens radius
lens_radius.name: lens_radius

light_filters.comment: Vector of LightFilters associated with the light.
light_filters.label: light filters
light_filters.name: light_filters

max_shadow_distance.comment: The distance from the light beyond which a light-receiving surface will no longer receive shadows cast from that light. Note that the distance is thresholded for each occlusion ray cast for this light, it is possible for a receiving point to lie at an intermediate distance such that some parts of the light are closer than the threshold distance and other parts beyond it, in which case the point will appearto be in partial shadow.
max_shadow_distance.name: max_shadow_distance

mb.comment: Whether motion-blur is active for this light. When set to true, the scene's illumination will correctly account for any blur() applied to the light's transformation matrix.
mb.name: mb

min_shadow_distance.comment: The distance from the light before which a light-receiving surface will no longer receive shadows cast from that light. Note that the distance is thresholded for each occlusion ray cast for this light, it is possible for a receiving point to lie at an intermediate distance such that some parts of the light are closer than the threshold distance and other parts beyond it, in which case the point will appearto be in partial shadow.
min_shadow_distance.name: min_shadow_distance

normalized.comment: When set to true, the size of the light can be changed without altering the amount of total energy cast into the scene. This is achieved via scaling the light's radiance by the reciprocal of its surface area. When set to false, the radiance is used as-is, regardless of surface area.
normalized.name: normalized

offset.comment: Per-channel offset used in tandem with a per-channel gain for color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel: output = input * gain + offset
offset.name: offset

on.comment: Whether the light is switched on.
on.name: on

outer_cone_angle.comment: The apex angle of the bounding cone of the light emitted by the SpotLight. No illumination takes placeoutside this angle. This is a full angle, measured from one side to the other. There is a falloff function applied between the outer and inner cones - see the angle_falloff_type attribute.
outer_cone_angle.label: outer cone angle
outer_cone_angle.name: outer_cone_angle

presence_shadows.comment: Switch this attribute on for shadows cast from this light to correctly respect presence values. When off, surfaces with a material with presence less than 1.0 will cast opaque shadows from this light. This is an optimization - when the attribute is off, occlusion rays (fast) are used for testing for shadows. When it is on, regular rays (slower) are used, and the material's presence is evaluated to determine how much shadowing should occur. When set to "use default" it reads from the value of SceneVariable enable_presence_shadows.
presence_shadows.label: presence shadows
presence_shadows.name: presence_shadows

ray_termination.comment: Whether the light is used for ray termination color. Ray termination color is used for filling in falsely dark areas where ray paths have been terminated too early by the depth controls. Such a ray path immediately exits to any ray termination light(s) present in the light set being applied to the lobe, ignoring occlusion by scene geometry. Any light can either be a regular light or a ray termination light (but not both). Thus they can be freely assigned to light sets, which provides a mechanism for applying specific ray termination lights to specific materials, parts or objects. Ray termination color is only applied to non-hair transmission lobes.
ray_termination.name: ray_termination

saturation.comment: Per-channel saturation used in color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel: output = lerp(luminance(inputRGB), input, saturation).
saturation.name: saturation

temperature.comment: Color temperature using Nuke-style T/M/I settings (T = temperature, M = magenta/green, I = intensity). This is achieved as follows: The 3-channel temperature is interpreted as the vector (T,M,I). The followiong scale values are then applied to the RGB components: outputR = inputR * (pow(2,I) + M/3 - T/2) outputG = inputG * (pow(2,I) - 2*M/3 outputB = inputB * (pow(2,I) + M/3 + T/2)
temperature.name: temperature

texture.comment: File name of the texture applied to the light. If set to the empty string, no texture is applied. Any file format supported by OpenImageIO can be used. The texture is used in 2 ways - for looking up the texture value at the intersection point when a ray hits the light, and for building a lookup-table-based auxilliary data structure used for distributing light samples over the texture.
texture.name: texture

texture_border_color.comment: RGB value used when a texture lookup occurs outside the texture.
texture_border_color.name: texture_border_color

texture_coverage.comment: Texture scales in the u and v-directions.
texture_coverage.name: texture_coverage

texture_filter.comment: The filtering mode to apply to the texture. Nearest neighbor is the cheapest filtering mode but produces a blocky result. Switch linear filtering on for a smoother result. Additionally, mip-mapping can be switched on with either nearest neighbor or linear filtering.
texture_filter.label: texture filter
texture_filter.name: texture_filter

texture_mirror_u.comment: Whether to mirror the texture in the u-direction. If set to false, the texture is repeated in the u-direction.
texture_mirror_u.name: texture_mirror_u

texture_mirror_v.comment: Whether to mirror the texture in the v-direction. If set to false, the texture is repeated in the v-direction.
texture_mirror_v.name: texture_mirror_v

texture_reps_u.comment: Number of times texture repeats in u over the scaled texture space.
texture_reps_u.name: texture_reps_u

texture_reps_v.comment: Number of times texture repeats in v over the scaled texture space.
texture_reps_v.name: texture_reps_v

texture_translation.comment: Translation of the texture in (u,v)-space, in units of the texture size. For example, a translation of (0.25, 0.5) will translate the texture one-quarter of its width in the u-direction and one-half of its height in the v-direction.
texture_translation.name: texture_translation

visible_diffuse_reflection.comment: Whether the light is visible in diffuse reflection.
visible_diffuse_reflection.label: visible diffuse reflection
visible_diffuse_reflection.name: visible_diffuse_reflection

visible_diffuse_transmission.comment: Whether the light is visible in diffuse transmission.
visible_diffuse_transmission.label: visible diffuse transmission
visible_diffuse_transmission.name: visible_diffuse_transmission

visible_glossy_reflection.comment: Whether the light is visible in glossy reflection.
visible_glossy_reflection.label: visible glossy reflection
visible_glossy_reflection.name: visible_glossy_reflection

visible_glossy_transmission.comment: Whether the light is visible in glossy transmission (refraction).
visible_glossy_transmission.label: visible glossy transmission
visible_glossy_transmission.name: visible_glossy_transmission

visible_in_camera.comment: Whether the light is directly visible in the scene's active camera. When set to "use default" it reads from the value of SceneVariable lights_visible_in_camera.
visible_in_camera.label: visible in camera
visible_in_camera.name: visible_in_camera

visible_mirror_reflection.comment: Whether the light is visible in miror reflection.
visible_mirror_reflection.label: visible mirror reflection
visible_mirror_reflection.name: visible_mirror_reflection

visible_mirror_transmission.comment: Whether the light is visible in miror transmission (refraction).
visible_mirror_transmission.label: visible mirror transmission
visible_mirror_transmission.name: visible_mirror_transmission

contains_camera.comment: Specifies whether the geometry contains the camera and should be used for IOR tracking. This should not be changed by the user -- they should instead attach the relevant geometry to the camera, which will then flag this geometry.
contains_camera.name: contains_camera

density_grid.comment: The name of the density grid. If multiple grids have the same name, only the first grid with that name will be loaded. If a vdb file has multiple grids with the same name, you may use a suffix index to pick which grid to load, e.g. "density[3]". The index must be in [] brackets.
density_grid.label: density grid
density_grid.name: density_grid

dicing_camera.comment: Alternate camera that is used for adaptive tessellation. This is useful if you want adaptive tessellation to behave consistently in a sequence, regardless of what the main camera is doing
dicing_camera.name: dicing_camera

emission_grid.comment: The name of the emission grid. If multiple grids have the same name, only the first grid with that name will be loaded. If a vdb file has multiple grids with the same name, you may use a suffix index to pick which grid to load, e.g. "emission[3]". The index must be in [] brackets.
emission_grid.label: emission grid
emission_grid.name: emission_grid

emission_sample_rate.comment: the relative scale of input emission grid resolution. Lower value has lower memory overhead and faster render time, with the cost of lower fidelity of emission shape and illumination
emission_sample_rate.label: emission sample rate
emission_sample_rate.name: emission_sample_rate

interpolation.comment: Voxel interpolation to use when sampling the volume data
interpolation.name: interpolation

label.comment: label used in material aov expresssions
label.name: label

modo_material.comment: The material tag of the Modo material this is rendered with; empty for the base material.
modo_material.label: material tag
modo_material.name: modo_material

modo_volume.comment: The name of a MoonRay volume item that fills this shape.
modo_volume.label: volume
modo_volume.name: modo_volume

ray_epsilon.comment: When a secondary ray is fired, anything within this distance of the intersection point will be ignored. Instead, it is considered part of the current intersection's geometry. If zero, an automatically calculated epsilon will be used.
ray_epsilon.label: ray epsilon
ray_epsilon.name: ray_epsilon

references.comment: list of geometries that geometry procedural can reference during procedural generate/update stages. For example, an instancer geometry procedural can instance primitives generated by the reference geometry procedural.
references.name: references

reverse_normals.comment: enable to reverse the normals in the geometry
reverse_normals.label: reverse normals
reverse_normals.name: reverse_normals

shadow_exclusion_mappings.comment: A space-separated list of mappings of the form A:B where: A is a comma-separated list of names of parts of this Geometry, or an asterisk to specify the whole geometry; B is a comma-separated list of shadow receiver set labels established using the ["shadow_receiver_label"] attribute, or an asterisk to specify to all such sets in the scene. For each of the listed mappings, shadows from the parts specified in A will be suppressed from casting onto any geometries in the ShadowReceiverSets specified in B. **Note: no part name should appear more than once in the string, otherwise the behavior is undefined.**
shadow_exclusion_mappings.name: shadow_exclusion_mappings

shadow_ray_epsilon.comment: When a shadow ray is fired, anything within this distance of the intersection point will be ignored. If this value is less than "ray_epsilon", then it has no additional effect.
shadow_ray_epsilon.label: shadow ray epsilon
shadow_ray_epsilon.name: shadow_ray_epsilon

shadow_receiver_label.comment: Label used to associate Geometry objects into ShadowReceiverSets. Using this in combination with the ["shadow_exclusion_mappings"] attribute, shadows from specified geometries or their parts can be suppressed from casting shadows onto one or more specified sets.
shadow_receiver_label.name: shadow_receiver_label

side_type.comment: set single sidedness of the mesh, will affect the visibility of the mesh based on normal direction
side_type.label: side type
side_type.name: side_type

static.comment: disable if the geometry will be updated between frames
static.name: static

use_local_camera_motion_blur.comment: Enables experimental feature that also attempts to remove the camera blur in the local regions
use_local_camera_motion_blur.label: use local camera motion blur
use_local_camera_motion_blur.name: use_local_camera_motion_blur

use_local_motion_blur.comment: Enables the local motion blur feature, which makes the geometry procedural responsible for handling all of the geometry's motion and allows for custom effects
use_local_motion_blur.label: use local motion blur
use_local_motion_blur.name: use_local_motion_blur

velocity_grid.comment: the name of vector grid representing the velocity field. Usually named "v" or "vel" in simulation export. If multiple velocity grids have the same name, only the first grid with that name will be loaded. If a vdb file has multiple grids with the same name, you may use a suffix index to pick which grid to load, e.g. "v[3]". The index must be in [] brackets. The index can be different from the index on the "density_grid".
velocity_grid.label: velocity grid
velocity_grid.name: velocity_grid

velocity_sample_rate.comment: the relative scale of input velocity grid resolution. Lower value has lower memory overhead and lower fidelity of motion blur effect, which is sometimes desired for artistic reasons
velocity_sample_rate.label: velocity sample rate
velocity_sample_rate.name: velocity_sample_rate

velocity_scale.comment: A scale factor for the velocity field. A value of 0 disables motion blur.
velocity_scale.label: velocity scale
velocity_scale.name: velocity_scale

visible_diffuse_reflection.comment: whether the geometry is visible in diffuse reflection
visible_diffuse_reflection.label: visible diffuse reflection
visible_diffuse_reflection.name: visible_diffuse_reflection

visible_diffuse_transmission.comment: whether the geometry is visible in diffuse transmission
visible_diffuse_transmission.label: visible diffuse transmission
visible_diffuse_transmission.name: visible_diffuse_transmission

visible_glossy_reflection.comment: whether the geometry is visible in glossy reflection.
visible_glossy_reflection.label: visible glossy reflection
visible_glossy_reflection.name: visible_glossy_reflection

visible_glossy_transmission.comment: whether the geometry is visible in glossy transmission (refraction).
visible_glossy_transmission.label: visible glossy transmission
visible_glossy_transmission.name: visible_glossy_transmission

visible_in_camera.comment: whether the geometry is visible to camera rays
visible_in_camera.label: visible in camera
visible_in_camera.name: visible_in_camera

visible_mirror_reflection.comment: whether the geometry is visible in miror reflection.
visible_mirror_reflection.label: visible mirror reflection
visible_mirror_reflection.name: visible_mirror_reflection

visible_mirror_transmission.comment: whether the geometry is visible in miror transmission (refraction).
visible_mirror_transmission.label: visible mirror transmission
visible_mirror_transmission.name: visible_mirror_transmission

visible_volume.comment: whether the geometry is visible in indirect volume rays
visible_volume.label: visible volume
visible_volume.name: visible_volume

blur_type.comment: The type of blur to apply
blur_type.name: blur_type

color_tint.comment: Tints the light filter. Lower density increases the shift toward the tint color.
color_tint.name: color_tint

density_grid_name.comment: The name of the grid within the .vdb file from which to sample for density(hint: use openvdb_print to see contents of .vdb file). If no grid is specified, it will use 'density' as the defaultIn cases where there are multiple grids with the same name, the grid name can be indexed (eg. density[1])
density_grid_name.label: density grid name
density_grid_name.name: density_grid_name

density_remap_input_max.comment: Clamp the remapped input to this max value
density_remap_input_max.label: density remap input max
density_remap_input_max.name: density_remap_input_max

density_remap_input_min.comment: Clamp the remapped input to this min value
density_remap_input_min.label: density remap input min
density_remap_input_min.name: density_remap_input_min

density_remap_inputs.comment: List of input remap curve values
density_remap_inputs.label: density remap input
density_remap_inputs.name: density_remap_inputs

density_remap_interpolation_types.comment: List of density remap interpolation types
density_remap_interpolation_types.label: density remap interpolation types
density_remap_interpolation_types.name: density_remap_interpolation_types

density_remap_output_max.comment: Clamp the remapped output to this max value
density_remap_output_max.label: density remap output max
density_remap_output_max.name: density_remap_output_max

density_remap_output_min.comment: Clamp the remapped output to this min value
density_remap_output_min.label: density remap output min
density_remap_output_min.name: density_remap_output_min

density_remap_outputs.comment: List of output remap curve values
density_remap_outputs.label: density remap outputs
density_remap_outputs.name: density_remap_outputs

invert_density.comment: Invert the density with density = 1 - density
invert_density.name: invert_density

vdb_interpolation_type.comment: The type of interpolation to use when sampling the filter
vdb_interpolation_type.name: vdb_interpolation_type

anisotropy.comment: Value in the interval [-1,1] that defines how foward (1) or backward (-1) scattering the volume is. A value of 0.0 indicates an isotropic volume.
anisotropy.name: anisotropy

bake_divisions.comment: Divide widest axis by this many divisions
bake_divisions.name: bake_divisions

bake_resolution_mode.comment: Method to specify grid resolution of baked density grid. Choices are: \t\t"default": For shaders that are bound to vdb volumes, use vdb resolution. \t\t\t\t\t\tFor shaders that are bounds to mesh geometries use 100 divisions \t\t"divisions": Specify number of divisions. \t\t"voxel size": Specify voxel size.
bake_resolution_mode.label: bake resolution mode
bake_resolution_mode.name: bake_resolution_mode

bake_voxel_size.comment: Size of voxel in world space
bake_voxel_size.name: bake_voxel_size

incandescence_gain_mult.comment: A multiplier applied to the volume emission
incandescence_gain_mult.label: incandescence gain mult
incandescence_gain_mult.name: incandescence_gain_mult

opacity_gain_mult.comment: A multiplier applied to the volume density
opacity_gain_mult.label: opacity gain mult
opacity_gain_mult.name: opacity_gain_mult

surface_opacity_threshold.comment: Accumulated opacity that's considered the 'surface' for computing surface position and Z
surface_opacity_threshold.name: surface_opacity_threshold
